answers.text: You can infer that the audience and white society never treated Truth like a fragile lady who needed protection. Truth directly points this out when she says, "Nobody ever helps me into carriages, or over mud-puddles, or gives me any best place!" This quote shows that nobody helped her over puddles or gave her good places, so she was treated totally different than white women.

The best detail from her life is her physical strength working on the farm. She told the crowd, "I have ploughed and planted, and gathered into barns, and no man could head me!" This detail is much more stronger than her detail about eating because working hard in the fields proves women are equal.

Her response to the religious argument is the most convincing one between the two points she makes. She challenges the preacher by saying, "Where did your Christ come from? From God and a woman!" This statement completely destroys the man's point because it shows that women are important in the Bible so they should have equal rights.

You can infer that the audience and people in general treated Truth with a lot less respect than white women back then. She supports this when she says, "Nobody ever helps me into carriages, or over mud-puddles, or gives me any best place!" This shows that nobody helped her over mud-puddles, which proves that the people around her never treated her nicely at all.

The strongest detail from her life is her physical labor because it proves she could match any male worker. She says I have ploughed and planted, and gathered into barns, and no man could head me to show how powerful she was. That detail is stronger than her having thirteen children because working outside in the dirt takes more strength than being a mother.

Her answer about Christ is more convincing because she uses religion against the man who tried to argue with her. Truth asks, "Where did your Christ come from? From God and a woman! Man had nothing to do with Him." This evidence is convincing because it shows that men had nothing to do with Jesus, which proves women should get rights.

We can infer that the audience did not treat Truth with chivalry or respect like they treated other ladies because of her race. Truth states, "Nobody ever helps me into carriages, or over mud-puddles, or gives me any best place!" This shows that nobody helped her over puddles, so the white men in the room were ignoring her speech and being disrespectful. Therefore, she was treated much worse than the white women who got helped into carriages.

The detail about her children being taken away is her strongest support because it creates a powerful emotional feeling. Truth says, "I have borne thirteen children, and seen most all sold off to slavery," which is much stronger than ploughing fields because back then women were not allowed to have large families without the government's permission. She also claims "no man could head me," but emotional pain from losing kids beats physical labor every time.

The answer about Christ is definitely the most convincing argument she makes to defend equality. She challenges the audience by saying, "Where did your Christ come from? From God and a woman!" This evidence proves that men had nothing to do with religion, so women should have all the power instead of men. Her pint cup argument is weaker because it just talks about drinks instead of giving a real point.
